attempts.entry_title: Morphology of the cervical and subdiaphragmatic vagus nerves of human, pig and rat (Pelot et al. 2020)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data: the nerve and fascicle diameters, fascicle numbers and tissue proportions of the human, pig and rat vagus at both levels, rat nerves about ten times smaller, and perineurium thickness rising with fascicle diameter. One did not: cervical and subdiaphragmatic perineurium fits differ in humans, even with samples taken into account, where the paper reports no difference and names no test. Cervical fascicles were larger in all three species, though the pig contrast was weaker (p = 0.012 against 0.0009). Comparisons with published values held in part. Minor claims on age trends, fat in pig nerves and one peanut fascicle count did not match.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Pelot, Goldhagen, Cariello, Musselman, Clissold, Ezzell and Grill (2020) on seven SPARC datasets, the binary traces of the rat (SPARC 60), pig (SPARC 64 and 89) and human (SPARC 65) vagus nerve sections and the Masson's trichrome micrographs of all collected samples (SPARC 16, 61 and 82). It measures nerve and fascicle diameters, fascicle counts, tissue proportions and perineurium thickness as the paper's deposited code does, refits the mixed model ANOVAs and Tukey tests, the perineurium fits and the Sunderland reanalysis, and judges three claims by eye on the micrographs.

outcomes.statement: Effective nerve diameter differs across species and across nerve levels, with no detected interaction of species and level.
outcomes.quote: The nerve diameter differed across species ( p < 0.0001; F = 577.1) and nerve levels ( p = 0.0030; F = 11.01), but we did not detect an interaction of species and level ( p = 0.1085; F = 2.445).

statistics.n: 9 cervical and 9 subdiaphragmatic samples per species (human, pig MT, rat)

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), variance unbounded (JMP's default; subject variance estimate negative), Kenward-Roger df: species F = 587.3 (p < 0.0001), level F = 11.03 (p = 0.0023), interaction F = 2.45 (p = 0.103), against 577.1, 11.01 (p = 0.0030) and 2.445 (p = 0.1085). Satterthwaite df give 599.6, 11.05 (p = 0.0029) and 2.45 (p = 0.108). Reading (b), bounded, puts the subject variance at zero and gives species F = 264.9, level F = 20.4 and a significant interaction (F = 3.60, p = 0.035); one reading is enough under the criterion. The rat traces of version 1 give the same reading (a) result (species F = 586.1).
deviations: Denominator degrees of freedom by Kenward-Roger, the claims file's (JMP's) method, implemented in mixed.py (no Python package has it), checked on balanced synthetic designs, where it gives the classical split-plot tests, and on the unbalanced fascicle diameter fit against finite differences; not checked against JMP. Satterthwaite df shown as a variant.
Rat nerve diameter is the outer perineurium of the largest fascicle (Methods, Imaging and Image Analysis, paragraph 3; DataPlotting_v4.m).

outcomes.statement: Effective fascicle diameter differs across species and nerve levels, with a significant species by level interaction.

outcomes.quote: At the subdiaphragmatic level, the fascicles diameters were comparable across all species ... although the human fascicles trended larger than the pig fascicles.
outcomes.notes: Subdiaphragmatic Tukey (Kenward-Roger df) human against pig p = 0.28, human against rat p = 1.00, pig against rat p = 0.88 (paper 0.3049, 0.896, 0.9947); with the rat fascicle the code keeps, 0.29, 0.898 and 0.995, the paper's order and within 0.002 of its values. Satterthwaite df shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: All three species have larger fascicles at the cervical than at the subdiaphragmatic level.
outcomes.quote: All species had larger fascicles at the cervical level ( p < 0.0001 for humans; p = 0.0009 for pigs; p = 0.0234 for rats).
outcomes.notes: Cervical larger in all species with Kenward-Roger df, the claims file's method: Tukey p < 0.00001 (human), 0.012 (pig, df 7.6) and 0.044 (rat); paper < 0.0001, 0.0009 and 0.0234. Satterthwaite df give 0.00001, 0.048 and 0.044; the rat fascicle the code keeps gives pig 0.013 and rat 0.0089. With containment df (16), a variant, rat p = 0.089. The pig and rat p values are larger than the paper's under every df method run, and the rat one is near 0.05 with the largest fascicle. On this unbalanced fit the Kenward-Roger quantities agree with finite differences (relative errors 1.6e-08 and 5.4e-07), and the KR df of each contrast equal 2v^2/(g'Wg) with the expected information; Satterthwaite's smaller df (pig 3.76) come from the observed information. The pig p of 0.012 against the paper's 0.0009 is not explained.
deviations: Denominator degrees of freedom by Kenward-Roger, the claims file's (JMP's) method, implemented in mixed.py (no Python package has it), checked on balanced synthetic designs, where it gives the classical split-plot tests, and on the unbalanced fascicle diameter fit against finite differences; not checked against JMP. Satterthwaite df shown as a variant.
Containment df (samples minus subjects minus 3) and the code's rat fascicle shown as variants.

outcomes.statement: The monofascicular rat nerves have diameters close to that of a single human or pig fascicle.
outcomes.quote: The monofascicular rat nerves were ∼10× smaller, and their diameters approximated the diameter of a single human or pig fascicle.
outcomes.notes: Rat mean nerve diameter 257.7 um lies between the pig and human mean fascicle diameters 154.5 and 354.8 um cervically, and 135.2 um between 110.1 and 163.5 um subdiaphragmatically (reading a); within the single-fascicle ranges 38.3 to 1060.5 and 6.8 to 587.1 um (reading b).

outcomes.statement: Endoneurium is a larger share of the human nerve cervically (32 +/- 7.9%) than subdiaphragmatically (8.8 +/- 5.3%), while in pigs it is more even across levels (27 +/- 5.3% and 20 +/- 4.0%, MT), slightly below the human cervical share and above the human subdiaphragmatic one; perineurium follows the same trends (human 8.9 +/- 2.5% and 3.4 +/- 1.6%, pig 5.1 +/- 1.8% and 4.0 +/- 0.5%).
outcomes.quote: The human endoneurium occupied a larger proportion of the nerve at the cervical level (32 ± 7.9%) than at the subdiaphragmatic level (8.8 ± 5.3%) whereas the endoneurial proportions were more consistent across levels in pigs, slightly lower than in the human cervical VN (27 ± 5.3% at the cervical level and 20 ± 4.0% at the subdiaphragmatic level for the MT micrographs ... These same trends between species and levels were present for the proportion of perineurium (8.9 ± 2.5% and 3.4 ± 1.6% at the cervical and subdiaphragmatic levels in humans; 5.1 ± 1.8% and 4.0 ± 0.5% in pigs).

Pig MT endoneurium is below human cervically (26.6 against 32.2) and above it subdiaphragmatically (20.3 against 8.8).

outcomes.statement: The pig endoneurial proportions from the anti-fibronectin IF micrographs are about 2 percentage points lower than those from MT, as the IF segmentation accounts for the perineurium.

outcomes.statement: In rats the ratio of mean subdiaphragmatic to mean cervical endoneurial area is 0.32 and the ratio of mean nerve diameters is 0.68.

outcomes.statement: Nerve and fascicle diameters are more consistent across samples in pigs (and rats) than in humans.
outcomes.quote: Qualitatively, the nerve and fascicle diameters were more consistent across samples for the pig nerves than for the humans nerves ( Figure 6 )
outcomes.notes: Coefficient of variation across samples, cervical and subdiaphragmatic: nerve diameter human 0.239 and 0.189, pig 0.089 and 0.099, rat 0.097 and 0.110; per-sample mean fascicle diameter human 0.314 and 0.662, pig 0.077 and 0.141, rat 0.098 and 0.109 (reading a); per-sample fascicle range human 0.500 and 0.853, pig 0.166 and 0.192 (reading b). Human exceeds pig and rat on every measure.

outcomes.statement: Pig vagus nerves are consistently oblong in cross section, whereas human nerves are more circular at the cervical level.
outcomes.quote: pig nerves were consistently oblong in shape, whereas the human samples were more circular at the cervical level ( Figures 2 , 3 , Supplement 3 )
outcomes.notes: Aspect ratio of the equal-moment ellipse: human cervical median 1.542, pig 2.459 to 4.285 cervically and 2.126 to 3.082 subdiaphragmatically; circularity human cervical median 0.654, pig 0.316 to 0.594. Every pig sample is less circular than the human cervical median under both readings, and the human cervical median is more circular than the pig median at each level. Human subdiaphragmatic nerves are as oblong as pig ones (median aspect 2.56).
deviations: Shape measured on the nerve traces (human inner trace for the four samples with two, as the code uses), with skimage regionprops (a standard choice).

outcomes.statement: Pig nerves have consistent collagenous epineurium, whereas many human subdiaphragmatic nerves have fatty extrafascicular tissue.
outcomes.quote: pig nerves had consistent collagenous epineurium, whereas many human subdiaphragmatic nerves had fatty extrafascicular tissue ( Supplement 3 )
outcomes.notes: By eye on the JPEG 2000 derivatives, adipose tissue in 29 of 32 human subdiaphragmatic micrographs, meeting both readings of many, but also within the epineurium of 13 of 45 pig micrographs (P5-1, P5-3, P6-1, P6-5, P6-7, P7-1, P7-5, P8-1, P8-3, P8-7, P9-3, P11-1, P13-1), where the criterion allows at most one. Full-resolution views with the authors' nerve traces of sparc-64 drawn over them show unilocular adipocytes inside the traced nerve in P11-1, P13-1, P5-1, P9-3 and P8-7 (65 to 84% of each region shown lies inside the trace; in P5-1 between fascicles). The contrast the paper draws holds in degree; the criterion's pig rule fails. Whether that rule reads the paper's comparative sentence is asked of a reader (questions/pelot-2020.yaml).
deviations: Judged by eye on compressed derivatives; the analysed pig samples with fat shown at full resolution with the nerve traces. The readings are recorded in pelot.py.
Supplement 3, which shows the paper's view of these sections, was not available.

outcomes.statement: In two pig cervical cross sections (P11-1 and P13-1) one fascicle contains cell bodies.
outcomes.quote: in two of the pig cervical cross sections, one fascicle contained cell bodies, although we did not sample the nerve close to the nodose ganglion
outcomes.notes: At full resolution, P11-1 (a fascicle at the upper edge) and P13-1 (the large fascicle at the left end) each have one fascicle holding large round somata with nuclei; none of the other seven shows one. The pale fascicles of P14-2, which the half-resolution view could not call, hold fibre profiles and no somata.
deviations: Judged by eye on the JPEG 2000 derivatives at full resolution; somata were not confirmed with a neuronal marker.

outcomes.statement: Human cervical fascicle numbers and endoneurial areas match prior reports while the nerve areas and diameters are generally smaller, so the endoneurial proportion is larger; human subdiaphragmatic sizes match prior reports, with fewer fascicles than one study of the posterior branch; pig fascicle numbers match literature, with slightly smaller mean diameters.
outcomes.quote: The numbers of fascicles and endoneurial cross-sectional areas of the human cervical VNs were comparable to previous reports, but the nerve cross-sectional areas and effective diameters were generally smaller, albeit with overlapping ranges.
outcomes.notes: Of 12 parts under the criterion's rules, 9 hold: human cervical fascicle numbers (all 7 literature means within 6.7 +/- 4.5), human cervical nerve area and diameter below all 7 studies (3.05 mm2, 1.92 mm), diameter below 3.0 mm, larger endoneurial proportion (32.2% against 10.8 and 12.9%), fewer human subdiaphragmatic fascicles than Stakenborg et al. (4.9 against 16), pig fascicle numbers (46 and 43 within 46.9 +/- 10.3 and 38.2 +/- 7.1) and smaller pig diameters (2.20 and 1.64 against 2.93 and 2.09 mm). Three fail: human cervical endoneurial area (0.92 +/- 0.34 mm2; the Seki et al. means 1.32 and 1.84 lie outside), overlapping ranges (six literature diameters without SD lie above our largest, 2.55 mm, though 6 of 7 areas overlap), and human subdiaphragmatic sizes, where the posterior-branch values of Tailai et al. and Gravgaard lie outside our mean +/- SD; the anterior-branch values, which the paper singles out, lie inside.
deviations: Literature means and SDs read from files/code/DataPlotting_v4.m of sparc-65 (the values Figure 7 plots, "see Supplementary Excel spreadsheet"), matched to the studies by the order of the Figure 7 legend; Supplement 4 itself was not available.

outcomes.statement: Rat cervical nerve diameters and areas agree with published data, while the rat subdiaphragmatic nerves are slightly larger than prior data.
outcomes.quote: The nerve diameters and cross-sectional areas of the rat cervical VNs compared well to published data, while our rat subdiaphragmatic nerves were slightly larger than prior data
outcomes.notes: The rat subdiaphragmatic mean (0.135 mm, 0.0145 mm2) is above all four Prechtl and Powley (1985) values, so that part holds. Of the three published cervical means, only the left VN of Licursi de Alcantara et al. (0.281 mm, 0.0620 mm2) lies within our 0.258 +/- 0.025 mm and 0.053 +/- 0.010 mm2; Fazan and Lachat (0.226 mm, 0.0635 mm2) and the right VN of Licursi de Alcantara et al. (0.299 mm, 0.0703 mm2) lie outside. Version 1 traces give the same counts.
deviations: Literature means and SDs read from files/code/DataPlotting_v4.m of sparc-65 (the values Figure 7 plots, "see Supplementary Excel spreadsheet"), matched to the studies by the order of the Figure 7 legend; Supplement 4 itself was not available.

outcomes.statement: For a given fascicle diameter, human fascicles have the thickest perineurium and rat fascicles the thinnest.
outcomes.quote: For a given fascicle diameter, the human samples had the thickest perineurium while the rat samples had the thinnest perineurium.
outcomes.notes: Fits with intercept (the code's poly1): human 0.0370 d + 10.5, pig IF 0.0255 d + 3.44, rat 0.0129 d + 1.37 um. Over the common range 32 to 284 um, human > pig > rat everywhere (reading a); at 250 um 19.8, 9.8 and 4.6 um (reading b). Zero-intercept fits give the same order.
deviations: Fit form from DataPlotting_v4.m and SegmentationAnalysis_v2.m (fittype poly1), which settles the claims file's open fit form.

outcomes.statement: The ratio of perineurium thickness to fascicle diameter decreases as fascicle diameter increases, particularly in humans and pigs.
outcomes.quote: The ratio of perineurium thickness to fascicle diameter decreased with increased fascicle diameter, particularly for the human and pig samples ( Figure 9B ).
outcomes.notes: Ratio implied by each fit falls over the species' range: human 1.583 to 0.047 (decrease 1.536), pig 0.265 to 0.037 (0.228), rat 0.056 to 0.018 (0.038), human and pig decreases larger than the rat's (reading a). Spearman of ratio with diameter -0.92, -0.60, -0.78 (reading b, pig weaker than rat).

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 73 human non-peanut fascicles has R2 = 0.75.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 73 human fascicles (excluding fascicles with more than one inner perineurium trace for a given outer perineurium trace, i.e., peanut fascicles) as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.75.
outcomes.notes: 73 non-peanut human fascicles; line with intercept R2 = 0.749 (0.0370 d + 10.5 um); zero-intercept R2 = 0.167 about the mean (0.865 uncentred).
deviations: Fit form poly1 from DataPlotting_v4.m (human fit block).

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 284 pig non-peanut fascicles (IF) has R2 = 0.30.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 284 pig non-peanut fascicles as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.30.
outcomes.notes: 284 non-peanut IF fascicles (counting, as bwboundaries does, the one hole trace in P13-3's inner mask); line with intercept R2 = 0.298 (0.0255 d + 3.44 um). Without that hole trace there are 285 fascicles and R2 = 0.301.
deviations: Fit form poly1 from SegmentationAnalysis_v2.m.

outcomes.statement: The fit of perineurium thickness against fascicle diameter for 22 rat fascicles has R2 = 0.77.
outcomes.quote: We fit the data from 22 rat fascicles as ... with d fasc in microns, yielding R 2 = 0.77.
outcomes.notes: All 22 rat fascicles (reading a, as DataPlotting_v4.m fits every rat fascicle with a thickness) with a line with intercept (reading i, the code's poly1): R2 = 0.765 (0.0129 d + 1.37 um). Other combinations: 18 largest with intercept 0.664, through zero 0.510 and 0.495. Version 1 traces give R2 = 0.570 for the 22.
deviations: Fascicle set and fit form taken from DataPlotting_v4.m.

outcomes.statement: In the human and pig vagus nerves, larger fascicles have thicker perineurium.
outcomes.quote: our data also showed thicker perineurium for larger fascicles, as well as thicker perineurium as a proportion of fascicle diameter for smaller fascicles.
outcomes.notes: Slopes 0.0370 (human, 95% CI 0.0319 to 0.0421) and 0.0255 (pig, 0.0209 to 0.0300); Spearman of thickness with diameter 0.92 and 0.54. Rat also positive (slope 0.0129, Spearman 0.86).

outcomes.statement: The relationship between perineurium thickness and fascicle diameter does not differ between cervical and subdiaphragmatic nerves in any of the three species.
outcomes.quote: The data did not suggest a difference in the relationship between perineurium thickness and fascicle diameter for cervical versus subdiaphragmatic nerves for any of the three species.
outcomes.notes: Human, cervical slope 0.0318 [0.0248, 0.0388] against subdiaphragmatic 0.0558 [0.0494, 0.0622], bounds do not overlap; F test of level terms F = 19.2, p < 0.0001. Pig, intercepts 5.26 [4.14, 6.39] against 3.16 [2.67, 3.65], bounds do not overlap; F = 21.0, p < 0.0001. Rat, bounds overlap, F = 0.14, p = 0.87 (version 1 traces F = 1.06, p = 0.37). Both readings detect a level difference in humans and pigs. Both treat fascicles as independent; with sample clustering (variant) the human difference remains (mixed model with a random intercept per sample chi2 = 28.7, p < 0.0001; errors clustered by sample F = 10.6, p = 0.0013) and the pig one does not (p = 0.58 and 0.26), so the pig difference rests on treating fascicles as independent and, with clustering, the outcome rests on the human fits alone. Asked of a reader (questions/pelot-2020.yaml).
deviations: The paper names no test for 'did not suggest a difference'; the claims file's tests are used.

outcomes.statement: Refitting all 777 fascicles of Sunderland and Bradley (1952) gives a zero-intercept slope of 2.75% of fascicle diameter for perineurium thickness, with R2 = 0.51.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraphs 13 and 14 (Eq. 4); Discussion, paragraph 7; Figure 9C and 9D
outcomes.quote: We re-analyzed the original ( Sunderland and Bradley, 1952 ) data, including all 777 fascicles ... and identified the slope of the best-fit line with zero intercept as 2.75% ( R 2 = 0.51)
outcomes.notes: On the 777 fascicles deposited in sparc-65 (files/code/Sunderland1984.mat, transcribed from Sunderland and Bradley 1952 Tables 1 to 4, per Sunderland1984_Plotting.m), the zero-intercept slope is 2.750% and R2 = 0.510 about the mean (reading a; uncentred 0.853).
deviations: The claims file gives these data as elsewhere with no archive identifier; they are deposited in sparc-65 version 8 and were read from there (listed under inputs).
outcomes.where: Sunderland and Bradley (1952), the published human somatic nerve fascicle measurements; no archive identifier

outcomes.statement: Rat perineurium thickness is close to the published 3% of fascicle diameter, slightly thicker for smaller fascicles and thinner for larger ones.
outcomes.quote: While we found that the rat perineurium thickness was similar to this published relationship, albeit slightly thicker for smaller fascicle diameters and thinner for larger fascicle diameters
outcomes.notes: Rat fit over the 3% line goes from 1.86 at 32 um to 0.59 at 284 um, within 0.5 to 2 and crossing once; against 2.75% it is 2.02 to 0.64, just outside the factor of two at the small end (the claim names 3%). Version 1 traces give 2.53 to 0.85 against 3%.
deviations: 'Similar' read as within a factor of two (claims file).

outcomes.statement: Human and pig vagal perineurium is substantially thicker than the 3% of fascicle diameter found for human somatic nerves, especially for smaller fascicles.
outcomes.quote: the human and pig perineurium was substantially thicker, especially for smaller fascicles ( Figure 9B )
outcomes.notes: Median thickness over diameter 0.095 (human) and 0.053 (pig); median excess over 0.03 below the median diameter 0.106 and 0.033, above it 0.038 and 0.016; 100% and 95% of fascicles above 3%.
deviations: The claims file's reading of 'substantially thicker, especially for smaller fascicles'.

outcomes.statement: Pig fascicle diameters from anti-fibronectin IF (14 to 303 um, mean 123, median 123, interquartile range 91 to 155 um) are consistent with those from MT (5 to 399 um, mean 135, median 130, interquartile range 96 to 168 um).
outcomes.quote: Note that the fascicle diameters for the pig anti-fibronectin IF ( Figures 9A,B ; 14 to 303 μm, mean = 123 μm, median = 123 μm, interquartile range = 91 to 155 μm) are consistent with the MT data ( Figure 6 ; 5 to 399 μm, mean = 135 μm, median = 130 μm, interquartile range = 96 to 168 μm).
outcomes.notes: IF (284 non-peanut), 14.4 to 302.8 um, mean 123.3, median 123.1, IQR 88.0 to 152.6. MT (766 traces), 23.7 to 399.1, mean 134.6, median 129.5, IQR 95.6 to 167.7. All four values within 10%, and the ranges and IQRs lie inside the reported ones widened by 10%, as the criterion reads. Read strictly, each bound within 10% of the paper's, the MT minimum fails (23.7 against 5 um). The version 1 masks of sparc-64 have a smallest trace of 4.7 um (mean 137.6, median 131.8), so the paper's 5 um minimum probably comes from them.
deviations: Quartiles by the Hazen definition, as MATLAB's prctile.

outcomes.statement: Human IHC micrographs have 60 cervical inner perineurium traces (27 bundles in 10 peanut fascicles) and 44 subdiaphragmatic (4 in 2); pig IF micrographs have 210 cervical (57 in 25) and 179 subdiaphragmatic (48 in 19).
outcomes.quote: For the human anti-claudin-1 IHC micrographs, the cervical level had 60 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 27 were intrafascicular bundles in 10 peanut fascicles; the subdiaphragmatic level had 44 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 4 were intrafascicular bundles in 2 peanut fascicles. For the pig anti-fibronectin IF micrographs, the cervical level had 210 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 57 were intrafascicular bundles in 25 peanut fascicles; the subdiaphragmatic level had 179 fascicles total (inner perineurium traces) of which 48 were intrafascicular bundles in 19 peanut fascicles.
outcomes.notes: Human 60 traces (27 bundles in 10 peanut fascicles) and 44 (4 in 2); pig IF 210 (57 in 24) and 179 (48 in 19). The four totals and three of the four peanut counts match; pig cervical has 24 peanut fascicles against 25 (P9-3 6, P11-1 4, P12-1 8, P14-2 6). No outer trace has a hole, no inner centroid lies in two outer traces and none is unmatched, and the non-peanut counts per sample equal those of PigIFMorphology.mat (284 in all); the deposited files do not record peanut groupings, so the 25 could not be traced.
deviations: Inner traces matched to outer traces by the centroid test of PerineuriumComplexMatch_v2.m; holes in inner masks counted as traces, as bwboundaries returns them.

outcomes.statement: The morphology metrics show no trend with age in any species.
outcomes.quote: Our morphology metrics did not show trends with age for any species ( Supplement 6 )
outcomes.notes: Pearson correlation with age per species, level and metric (27 tests), 3 with p < 0.05, all pig (cervical endoneurial % r = -0.72, p = 0.029; subdiaphragmatic nerve diameter r = 0.75, p = 0.019; subdiaphragmatic mean fascicle diameter r = 0.69, p = 0.039); 1.4 expected by chance. Spearman (variant) gives 1 (human subdiaphragmatic mean fascicle diameter, p = 0.041). Pig ages take four values, 10.5 to 15 weeks. Corrected over the 27 tests none is below 0.05 (smallest Holm-adjusted p 0.52, Benjamini-Hochberg 0.35; within pigs, Holm 0.15); the criterion counts uncorrected tests. Asked of a reader (questions/pelot-2020.yaml).
deviations: Supplement 6 was not available; the paper's code (DataPlotting_v4.m) only plots metrics against age, so the test is the claims file's choice, uncorrected for multiple tests.

outcomes.statement: The rat cervical carotid sheath holds up to six fascicles, of which the largest, taken as the vagus, was segmented.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 6 (Supplementary Figure 16); Materials and Methods, Imaging and Image Analysis, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The rat cervical VN was identified as monofascicular in prior studies ( Fazan and Lachat, 1997 ; Licursi de Alcântara et al., 2008 ), but we observed up to six fascicles within the carotid sheath ( Supplementary Figure 16 ).
outcomes.notes: Re-read at full resolution for the nine analysed left cervical sections of sparc-16 (shown at half resolution, bundles numbered): 2, 5, 5, 2, 3, 5, 4, 6, 2 bundles (R16-3 to R25-3); the largest count is six (R24-3), every section has more than one, and the bundle traced as the vagus is the largest in each. Eight small profiles that could not be told from a vessel are marked and not counted; counting them would raise R17-3 and R18-1 to six and none above six. The right sections keep their thumbnail counts (at most five). The first reading, on thumbnails, found at most five.
deviations: Judged by eye on the JPEG 2000 derivatives (the left sections at full resolution); Supplementary Figure 16 was not available. Readings and bundle positions recorded in pelot.py (RAT_SHEATH_FULLRES).

findings.statement: The readmes of sparc-60 and sparc-16 give the rats' ages as 65 to 268 days; the subjects sheets give 75 to 268 days, as the paper does.

outcomes.note: Both fit the same unbounded REML model with Kenward-Roger tests; on the expected information both get pig p = 0.012 (df 7.6) and rat 0.044, three species, and on the observed information pelot-2020-01 gets pig p = 0.055 (df 3.74), two species. pelot-2020-01 chose the observed information because it gives the paper's nerve diameter F values (577.0, 11.01, 2.4455 against 577.1, 11.01, 2.445), but neither choice gives the paper's pig p of 0.0009.

pelot-2020-01 blocked it because the criterion then said both that the claim was testable with the cervical micrographs and not testable when only the vagus is traced; the criterion was rewritten for pelot-2020-02 to be tested by eye on the micrographs whether or not the other bundles are traced. Under it pelot-2020-02 counted 2 to 6 bundles in the nine left sections at full resolution (5 at most on thumbnails), a judgement by eye that pelot-2020-01 did not make.

The verifier read the file lists and metadata of the archive for the blocked claims and tested mixed.fit and mixed.anova on a balanced synthetic split-plot. It had no attempt record and took the claims from the claims file; its outcomes agree with all 43 of the record's at that time.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2: the full executed notebook with its conclusions and summary, the helper modules pelot.py and mixed.py (including mixed._kr and kr_test), the claims file, the attempt record and the README, with the paper's full text. Its cell numbers refer to that notebook; this revision adds two data-check cells, so later cells are numbered two higher.

paper_notes.statement: The Discussion's rat ratio of subdiaphragmatic to cervical nerve diameter (0.68) is reproduced only with the connective tissue boundary for the three multifascicular samples (0.678), while the Results' rat means, which use the largest fascicle as the Methods state, give 0.52.

Questions for the authors. (1) Which JMP settings gave the mixed model F tests: the nerve diameter interaction is non-significant only with an unbounded (negative) subject variance, and the per-species fascicle diameter contrasts (fascicles-larger-cervical) are weaker here than in the paper under every df method (pig p = 0.012 with Kenward-Roger, 0.0016 with containment df; paper 0.0009). (2) What test, if any, supports 'did not suggest a difference' between levels in the perineurium fits; separate cervical and subdiaphragmatic fits differ in humans and pigs (F about 20, p < 0.0001), in humans also with sample clustering. (3) Whether Supplement 6 tested age trends; 3 of 27 Pearson correlations have p < 0.05 in pigs, none after correction. (4) The rule for counting carotid sheath bundles (Supplementary Figure 16) and for calling adipose tissue (Supplement 3).

The Methods take the largest rat fascicle, but DataPlotting_v4.m sorts only the outer perineurium diameters (FascicleOut) and keeps FascicleIn{1}, the inner trace of the first ring in bwboundaries order, as the rat fascicle diameter. In R22-1 and R23-1 that ring is not the largest (R22-1, 39.3 um against 105.8 um). The paper's rat fascicle values (0.121 +/- 0.032 mm subdiaphragmatically) follow the code (121.1 +/- 32.3 um), not the Methods (129.1 +/- 14.0 um), and so do its subdiaphragmatic Tukey p values with rats (0.898 and 0.995 with the code's fascicle, paper 0.896 and 0.9947). Its other rat Tukey p values follow neither selection closely (rat cervical against subdiaphragmatic 0.0089 with the code's fascicle and 0.044 with the largest, paper 0.0234; rat against pig cervically 0.14 with the code's fascicle, paper 0.1707).

The literature values of Figure 7 (Supplement 4) are also hard-coded in the paper's plotting code (DataPlotting_v4.m, deposited in sparc-60, 64 and 65) with reference numbers that match the Figure 7 legend order, so they can be read from the datasets without the supplement.

entries.name: pelot-2020
entries.title: Morphology of the cervical and subdiaphragmatic vagus nerves of human, pig and rat (Pelot et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Pelot, Goldhagen, Cariello, Musselman, Clissold, Ezzell and Grill (2020) on seven SPARC datasets, the binary traces of the rat (SPARC 60), pig (SPARC 64 and 89) and human (SPARC 65) vagus nerve sections and the Masson's trichrome micrographs of all collected samples (SPARC 16, 61 and 82). It measures nerve and fascicle diameters, fascicle counts, tissue proportions and perineurium thickness as the paper's deposited code does, refits the mixed model ANOVAs and Tukey tests, the perineurium fits and the Sunderland reanalysis, and judges three claims by eye on the micrographs.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pelot et al. (2020) from seven SPARC datasets
Earlier findings of pelot-2020-01, checked on these versions

papers.title: Quantified Morphology of the Cervical and Subdiaphragmatic Vagus Nerves of Human, Pig, and Rat
